stories.headline: Graduate visa cut to 18 months from 1 January 2027
stories.seoTitle: Graduate visa cut to 18 months from 2027
stories.description: From 1 January 2027, new Graduate visas will last 18 months instead of two years. Here's who it affects, the key dates and what stays the same.
stories.summary: From 1 January 2027, new Graduate visas will last 18 months instead of two years. Here are the key dates and what stays the same.
stories.intro: If you're an international student hoping to stay in the UK after your course, there's a date worth knowing. From 1 January 2027, new Graduate visas will last 18 months instead of two years.

p: The Graduate visa lets you stay in the UK after you finish your course. At the moment it lasts two years. If you apply on or after 1 January 2027, it will last 18 months.

list: Apply on or before 31 December 2026: your visa lasts 2 years
Apply on or after 1 January 2027: your visa lasts 18 months
PhD or other doctoral qualification: your visa lasts 3 years either way

p: You can apply once your university or college has told the Home Office you've completed your course. You don't have to wait until your graduation ceremony or until you get your certificate. You must be in the UK when you apply, and you must apply before your Student visa expires.
So if your course ends around the new year, the date your university confirms you've finished could make a difference to how long your visa lasts.

list: You still can't extend a Graduate visa, but you may be able to switch to another visa, such as a Skilled Worker visa.
The application fee is £937, plus the healthcare surcharge, which is usually £1,035 for each year of your visa (as listed on gov.uk at the time of writing).

stories.headline: Student visa savings requirement rises on 30 November 2026
stories.seoTitle: Student visa savings rise on 30 November 2026
stories.description: The Student visa financial requirement rises on 30 November 2026: £1,570 a month in London and £1,203 a month elsewhere. Here are the details.
stories.summary: The money you must show for a Student visa is going up: £1,570 a month in London and £1,203 a month elsewhere.
stories.intro: If you're planning to apply for a UK Student visa, the amount of money you need to show is going up. The new amounts take effect on 30 November 2026.

p: When you apply for a Student visa, you usually have to show you have enough money to support yourself, on top of your course fees. The monthly amounts are rising:
list: Courses in London: from £1,529 to £1,570 a month
Courses outside London: from £1,171 to £1,203 a month

p: The new amounts take effect on 30 November 2026. Applications made before then are decided under the rules in force on 29 November 2026.

list: You show the monthly amount for up to 9 months.
You must have held the money for at least 28 days in a row.
If you've been living in the UK with a visa for at least 12 months before you apply, you don't need to show this money.

p: If you're planning to apply for a Student visa for a new course, check the current figures on gov.uk before you apply.

stories.headline: Skilled Worker visas: IT is the top job as hospitality falls 76%
stories.seoTitle: Skilled Worker visas in 2026: the top jobs
stories.description: IT professionals got the most Skilled Worker visas in the year to June 2026, while hospitality fell 76%. See which jobs are still sponsored and why.
stories.summary: IT is still the most common job on the Skilled Worker visa, while hospitality visas fell 76% after over 100 jobs stopped qualifying.
stories.intro: If you're an international student or graduate hoping to work in the UK, it helps to know which jobs still get sponsored. New Home Office figures show IT is still the most common job on the Skilled Worker visa, while hospitality has fallen sharply.

p: The Skilled Worker visa is the main UK work visa. It needs an employer with a sponsor licence. In the year to June 2026:
list: 26,894 visas went to main applicants (the person with the job), 30% fewer than the year before
IT professionals got 4,674 of these, 7% fewer, but still more than any other job
Food preparation and hospitality got 528, down 76%, which was most of the fall

p: From 22 July 2025, the skill level needed for the Skilled Worker visa went up. The Home Office says over 100 jobs are no longer eligible as a result, so there are fewer applications and visas.
Newer monthly figures show the fall is continuing. In the year to September 2026, there were 26,400 Skilled Worker applications from main applicants, 43% fewer than the year before.

Many people on work visas started out as students. Of everyone granted a work visa extension in 2025, 40% had been on a study visa before. Most of them moved from a Student visa to the Graduate visa first.
The September figures also show 352,500 Student visa applications from main applicants in the year to September 2026, 19% fewer than the year before.
For the Graduate visa, in the year to June 2026:
list: 157,356 Graduate visa extensions were granted, 39% fewer than the year before
most of that fall came from an 81% drop in visas for dependants (family members)

p: These are Home Office statistics, not rule changes. The monthly figures are provisional, and the next update is due on 12 November 2026. You can see the full figures on gov.uk.
